KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Hoop Toss — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches hoop toss — the ring game where every peg is worth a different number of points.

What is this?

Hoop toss is a throwing game: toss the rings so they land around the pegs, and the peg you ring decides your points.

What does it mean?

Choosing your target is the real lesson — the near peg is easy for 10, the far peg is hard for 50, and every turn is a small brave decision.

What does the child need to know?

You need rings (or jar lids, or paper plates with the middle cut out) and pegs or bottles to ring — near ones and far ones.

Why this matters

Scoring gives the game a story: tallies on paper, totals to add, a champion to crown — the math rides inside the game.

What it teaches

Flat-ring throwing, target choice, tally marking, and adding round numbers by tens.

Words to learn

hoopringtosspegpointstallychampion

Say this to your child

“"Hold the ring flat. Choose your peg — the near one is easy, the far one is fifty! Let it fly flat... does it ring?"”

Step by step

  1. Set the pegs out — one close, one far, and one in the middle.
  2. Say the worth: near peg 10, middle 20, far 50 (the card&rsquo;s rings count by tens).
  3. Hold the ring flat, like a frisbee, elbow relaxed.
  4. Toss it flat and gentle — a spinning ring lands ringed.
  5. Tally your points on paper — one mark per ten — and add them up after five rounds.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the stand shows four scoring rings — 10, 20, 30 and 50 — with three hoops lying on the ground waiting for their turn to fly.

Ask your child

"Which peg will you aim for, and why?" "How many tens is 30?" "What is your plan for the fifty?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might go safe-and-steady on the ten peg every round, or spend all five throws chasing the fifty — both are honest strategies, and the tallies will tell the story.

Out in the real world

Ring toss stands appear at every fair and every school fête with the same rule — and the tally-adding you practice here is the same math the ticket booth does.

Try it together

Champion rules: five rings each, add the tallies, crown the champion, immediate rematch. Backwards round: the far peg is worth 10 and the near one is worth 50 — everything flips.

Understanding check

Ask: "How do we hold the ring?" (flat, like a frisbee) "Which peg is worth the most?" (the far one — fifty)

This lesson pairs with the Hoop Toss flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kids Games.
